title: Benchmarking the Evolution of Performance and Energy Efficiency Across Recent Generations of Intel Xeon Processors
problem: Recent Intel Xeon processor generations introduce novel architectural features such as on-package HBM and differentiated performance/efficiency variants. There is a need to systematically evaluate how these architectural innovations impact performance and energy efficiency across bandwidth-bound HPC workloads.
motivation: Understanding performance and energy efficiency trends across processor generations helps HPC practitioners and system designers make informed decisions about processor selection and workload optimization.
method: The researchers benchmarked four Intel Xeon processor generations (Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids, Granite Rapids, and Sierra Forest) using bandwidth-bound applications—workloads that slow down waiting for data from memory rather than due to processor speed. They measured the runtime and energy consumption of each processor, then compared results across generations to evaluate the impact of new features like on-package HBM (high-speed memory built into the processor) and efficiency-focused processor variants.
key_novelty: This work provides a comprehensive empirical benchmark of recent Intel Xeon processor generations, including models with on-package HBM and efficiency-focused variants, on bandwidth-bound applications.
contributions: Benchmarking of four recent Intel Xeon processor generations and variants
Performance and energy efficiency comparison across architectural designs
Evaluation of on-package HBM impact in HPC applications
Systematic analysis of performance-oriented versus efficiency-oriented processor trade-offs
limitations: Scope limited to bandwidth-bound HPC applications; generalizability to compute-bound workloads not discussed.
primary_theme: CPU processor generation benchmarking and efficiency analysis
